title: Humanoid Robot Performs Pig Surgery Under Remote Control
source_used: Streamline Feed (reporting on a Nature study)
key_facts: Researchers led by UC San Diego, published in Nature, used a Unitree G1 humanoid (nicknamed Surgie) for two pig gallbladder removals
A surgeon controlled it remotely from a console; it was not autonomous
Console-control times were 56 min 15 s and 31 min 59 s; the robot was repositioned or recalibrated 8 and 4 times
In a peg-transfer test the humanoid took about 560 s versus 118 s for the da Vinci Xi surgical robot
Authors list latency (about 156 ms), calibration, sterility and overheating as open problems
quote_evidence: A humanoid robot has completed two laparoscopic gallbladder removals in pigs, but the experiment was not autonomous surgery.
It is a preclinical feasibility demonstration—not evidence that humanoids are ready to operate on people or replace surgical teams.
why_it_matters_hint: A general-purpose humanoid did live animal surgery under human remote control, but is far from human use.
notes: Journal and publication date not confirmed beyond the article's statements (it mentions both Nature and a Nature Medicine highlight).
